correctness.rationale: For every positive state and |epsilon|<=1/2, direct rational subtraction proves the exact positive multiplier (5) for U. The log(1+z) remainder bound gives per-step error at most 4 epsilon^2. Reciprocal total density satisfies an affine contraction with forcing at most |epsilon|/a, leading to the displayed all-time error (1). At n of order epsilon^{-1}log(1/epsilon), this error vanishes. Algebraic inversion of U=w^2/(1-w^2), monotonicity and one-step O(epsilon) overshoot establish the two profiles and both sharp first-passage constants. All quantifiers, initial asymmetry and threshold regimes are explicit. Sixty exact Fraction tests and 14,448 drift checks were run, but the unbounded and limiting claims rest entirely on these analytic arguments.

value.rationale: The classical two-species competition stability exchange leaves an intrinsic dynamical question unanswered: how many generations does a near-neutral population composition stay close to coexistence before one competitor becomes dominant, or conversely approach balanced coexistence? The uniform log-odds bound holds for arbitrary total-density transients and resolves the critical logarithmically enhanced delay for any vanishing power-law initial asymmetry, with sharp constants on both sides and a nonconstant nonlinear sigmoid profile. This is a structural time-resolved theorem rather than another equilibrium classification, textbook local eigenvalue calculation, arbitrarily selected finite parameter table, or single-step estimate. Its specialization and historical-priority risks are disclosed.
